competences: The learner identifies key facts about qualities of a good leader — part b.
The learner explains how leaders are selected and the qualities expected of them.
languageCompetence: Pronounce, spell and read election, appointment, inheritance, volunteer, ballot, leader and leadership.
objectives: By the end of the lesson learners should name facts relating to qualities of a good leader — part b.
By the end of the lesson learners should answer the sourced exercise questions accurately.
priorKnowledge: Learners have studied civic, political, cultural and voluntary leaders during earlier SST lessons.
materials: P4 SST source notes on leadership
references: Primary 4 Social Studies Notes for Terms 1–3

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls earlier lessons about district leadership and introduces qualities of a good leader — part b by asking "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader.". They identify pupils' prior knowledge and set the objective.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied district leaders, answer the opening question and state what they know about choosing leaders.

steps.content: Good leaders are capable of doing their duties. Good leaders should be kind to people. Good leaders should respect other people. Good leaders should be knowledgeable. Good leaders should be approachable. Good leaders should take responsibility. Good leaders should work hard. Good leaders should be tolerant. Good leaders should be cooperative. Good leaders should set a good example. Good leaders should be confident. Good leaders should obey lawful instructions.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher presents the documented points for "Remember", including "Good leaders are capable of doing their duties. Good leaders should be kind to people." They check understanding using "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders." and explain the correct response.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners identify the leadership roles or election methods, respond to questions, and copy the referenced notes into their books.

steps.content: 5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader. | 4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders. | 1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong. | 3. Give any three roles played by cultural leaders in your community. | 2. Apart from the kings, mention any two other examples of cultural leaders in your
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher sets the original questions "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader." and "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders." and supervises individual written answers. They mark and correct the responses using the source references.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners write answers independently, compare them with class notes and correct any inaccurate points after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the main ideas and checks progress with "1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong." and "3. Give any three roles played by cultural leaders in your community.". They assign the remaining sourced question as homework.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer final oral questions, explain a relevant fact and record the original homework question.

assessment: Assess learners with "5. Mention any four qualities of a good leader.", "4. Give any four ways people in your district become leaders.", and "1. Name the type of leaders to which kings belong.". Mark the answers according to the lesson notes.
